transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… yeah. I’m here because I keep having these nights where I eat so much it honestly scares me. It usually starts after work, like after I’ve been grading papers or getting things ready for my class, and I’ll tell myself I’m just going to have some leftovers or a snack because I’m tired. But then it kind of keeps going.

Like, I’ll have the leftovers, and then cereal, and then crackers, and then I’ll be standing there eating peanut butter from the jar, and then I’ll remember I have snacks packed for my classroom and I’ll go through those too. It’s not just feeling hungry or having a big dinner. It feels like this amount of food that… I don’t know, it frightens me afterward, because it’s so much more than I meant to eat.
Can you tell me more about those times when you're eating — do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating once you start?

Yes. That’s probably the part that scares me the most, honestly. It really does feel like once I start, I’m not… in charge of it in the normal way.

Like, I’ll have this very clear thought of, Okay, Joan, stop now, you’ve had enough, put it away, and it’s almost like the reasonable teacher part of me — the part that can manage a classroom and make lesson plans and be organized — is standing off to the side watching me do it. And that part is saying, Stop, this is too much, you’re going to feel awful. But my hands just keep moving. I keep opening cabinets, opening packages, going back to the fridge, putting food in my mouth even though I’m not really choosing it anymore.

And I’ll try to make these little deals with myself, like, This is the last bowl, or Just finish this and then you’re done, but then I’m right back up again getting something else. It feels automatic, like I can’t interrupt it. I don’t usually stop because I decide to stop. I stop when I’m so full it hurts, like physically painfully full, and then I’m just sitting there thinking, What did I just do?
Do you feel upset or distressed about these eating episodes, or have they started to affect your daily life in any way?

Yes… very much. I mean, I feel upset right after, obviously, but it’s not only that moment anymore. It’s like my whole evening becomes about dealing with what happened with food, or trying to make up for it somehow, or worrying about when it’s going to happen again.

And then it spills into everything else. I’ll have grading I need to do for my students, and normally I’m very on top of that, but lately I’ll sit there with the stack of papers and I’m just… slow. Distracted. Tired. My mind keeps going back to what I ate, or what I need to do to feel okay again, and then I get behind. Then I’m up late trying to catch up, and the next day at school I’m trying so hard to look normal and put-together, like I’m still the organized teacher everyone expects.

Weekends are bad too, because instead of feeling like a break, they feel planned around food or undoing food. I’ll avoid making plans with friends, or I’ll go but I’m not really there. I’m thinking about whether they can tell something is wrong, or whether I seem different. So yes, it’s affecting my life. More than I want to admit, honestly.
Do these eating episodes usually happen when you're feeling stressed, upset, or dealing with negative emotions?

I’m… not completely sure. I mean, I want to say yes because that would make it feel more understandable, like there’s a clear reason for it, but I haven’t been able to pin it down that neatly.

Sometimes I’m tired after work, or kind of wound up from the day, but I don’t always feel obviously upset right before it happens. It’s not always like I have a fight with someone or I’m crying and then I eat. A lot of the time it’s more vague than that — like I’m drained, or restless, or just sort of… done with holding everything together. But I don’t know if that counts as stress or negative emotions exactly.

I’ve tried to look back afterward and figure out, What was I feeling before this started? And sometimes I can’t really answer. I just remember being in the kitchen, thinking I’d have something small, and then suddenly it’s become this whole thing. So I guess I haven’t noticed a clear pattern yet. There may be one, but I don’t feel like I understand it.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever make yourself vomit, take laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to make up for the food you ate?

I don’t usually make myself vomit, no. And I don’t take laxatives. But I do… I do other things that are probably not okay, if I’m being honest.

After one of those nights, I’ll wake up and feel this panic, like I have to undo it somehow. So I’ll tell myself I’m not allowed to eat breakfast, and then once I’m at school I’ll tell myself I’m not allowed to eat lunch either. I’ll pack something sometimes, just so it looks normal, or because part of me thinks maybe I’ll be reasonable that day, but then I’ll just leave it sitting there. And I’ll be teaching and trying to act normal, but I’m thinking, You can’t eat, not after what you did last night.

And then after school, instead of going home and resting like a normal person, I’ll go out on the trail and stay there for hours. Sometimes I’ll keep going even when I’m shaky or exhausted, because stopping feels like I’m failing at fixing it. Or I’ll come home and do extra yoga, not in a calm way, not like it’s actually good for me — more like I’m forcing myself through it because I feel like I have to earn being okay again.

It’s embarrassing to say that out loud, because I know it sounds extreme. In my head at the time it feels necessary, like the only way to make the guilt quiet down.
How often do these eating episodes happen? Would you say they occur at least once a week on average?

Yes… definitely at least once a week. I think that’s part of what scares me, because for the past few months it’s been rare to have a week where it doesn’t happen at all.

It’s usually one night where I start eating more than I planned, and then it just keeps going, and by the end I’m sitting there thinking, How did I let it get this bad again? And then the next day becomes about trying to compensate for it. I’ll go to school and tell myself I’m not going to eat there, or I’ll avoid what I brought, and then later I’ll make myself do a really long walk or extra yoga.

So… yes. It’s not every single night, but it’s frequent enough that I almost expect it now, like I’m waiting for the week to have that one bad night. And then the day after is usually ruined by trying to make up for it.
During these eating episodes, do you feel that you are no longer in control of what or how much you're eating?

Yes. That’s probably the part that scares me the most, honestly, because it doesn’t feel like normal overeating or just making a bad choice and then regretting it.

It’s like once I start, something switches. The reasonable part of me — the part that can stand in front of a classroom all day and keep things organized and be responsible — is still there, but it feels far away. Like I’m watching myself from the outside, almost. I’ll be thinking, Joan, stop. You don’t even want this anymore. You’re going to feel awful. And at the same time my hands are still opening things, still going back to the cabinet or the fridge, still putting food in my mouth.

I’ll tell myself, Okay, this is the last thing, and then it isn’t. Or I’ll try to put something away, and then a few minutes later I’m getting it back out. It feels almost automatic, like my body is doing it before I’ve fully decided to. And I keep going even after I’m not enjoying it, even after I feel too full. Sometimes I’m painfully full and I still feel like I can’t stop until it’s just… over, somehow.

So yes. I do feel out of control during it. Not the whole day, but once it gets going, it feels like I’ve lost the ability to make myself stop.
